audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Suzuki centralizers in the selected basis; edge slides require different edge orbits; an unstated path-component condition
limitations: F1 — Counterevidence: The abstract centralizer type and dimension were correct. With internal reversal conjugations restored, an explicit C satisfies every needed property. No counterexample to the existential Proposition7.10 or TheoremsA/B.
F2 — Counterevidence: Proposition3.10 rearranges distinct edge orbits, including the two Suzuki edge orbits of equal type; no failed use in the main proof was identified.

F3 — Counterevidence: The second assertion explicitly assumes a connected double centralizer, which the counterexample does not meet. All actual main applications use connected U(m) and connected centralizers/double centralizers.

proposition.claim:
In the chosen global-antidiagonal basis the dihedral centralizer is printed as diag(a1,...,as,as,...,a1,b), and C has final identity block I1.

Orbit edge slide preserves G-homotopy type under stabilizer inclusion with no different-orbits hypothesis.

Vertex constants can be inserted/deleted by homotopy for a general Lie target, without a component hypothesis.

Let P=diag(a1,...,as). Correct H=diag(P,J_N P J_N,b). Take D=diag(I_N,J_N,I_h), C=A^-1 D A. Then AYA^-1=diag(I_N,-I_(N+h)), C centralizesY, A^-1 K A is contained in C(Y), and AC=1/sqrt2[[I,J],[J,-I]] direct-sumI_h commutes with the full correctedH. Dimensions give gap q(q-2)/4>0. General proof in report section2.

Require G.e != G.e'. Retained e provides the attaching-endpoint homotopy; Ge' subsetGe ensures it is equivariant; attachment along homotopic maps gives the conclusion.

For first assertion require rho0(g) in the identity component of the target, or connected target. For quotient version require path in identity component of double centralizer; printed connectedness already suffices.
